2027-05-23.title: The Most Holy Trinity
readings: The Lord is God in heaven above and on the earth beneath; there is no other
Blessed the people the Lord has chosen to be his own
You have received a spirit of adoption. When we cry, “Abba! Father!”
Baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit
2027-05-23.alt: Solemnity, Year B. Gloria and Creed. The Sunday after Pentecost is kept as the Solemnity of the Most Holy Trinity, and it takes the place of the Eighth Sunday in Ordinary Time this year. The Angelus is prayed at noon. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-05-23.verse: Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
theo: Last Sunday the Easter season ended with the outpouring of the Holy Spirit. Today the Church pauses and looks at the whole mystery that Easter and Pentecost have revealed: the one God who is Father, Son and Holy Spirit. This is not a puzzle invented by theologians. It is the name into which every one of us was baptised, and the Church calls it “the central mystery of Christian faith and life” (CCC 234). The first reading prepares the ground. Moses, at the end of the desert years, asks Israel to look back over all history: “ask now about former ages, long before your own, ever since the day that God created human beings on the earth; ask from one end of heaven to the other: has anything so great as this ever happened or has its like ever been heard of?” Has any people heard the voice of God speaking out of the fire and lived? Has any god gone to take a nation for himself “by a mighty hand and an outstretched arm”? Israel's God is not a distant idea but the God who speaks and acts, who chooses and rescues. And from that history comes the confession that stands at the root of our faith: “So acknowledge today and take to heart that the Lord is God in heaven above and on the earth beneath; there is no other.” Christians do not believe in three gods. The Trinity is the one God of Israel, revealed in his innermost life.

The Psalm sings of this God who creates by his word and his breath: “By the word of the Lord the heavens were made, and all their host by the breath of his mouth.” The Fathers of the Church loved this verse, for in it they heard, quietly hidden in the Old Testament, the Word and the Spirit of the Father at work in creation. The Lord is the God whose “word is upright,” who “loves righteousness and justice,” whose “steadfast love” fills the earth; and his eye is “on those who fear him, on those who hope in his steadfast love.” So the people can say: “Our soul waits for the Lord; he is our help and shield.” The refrain gathers it up: blessed the people the Lord has chosen to be his own.

St Paul, in the Letter to the Romans, shows that the Trinity is not only a truth to be believed but a life into which we are drawn. “For all who are led by the Spirit of God are children of God. For you did not receive a spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you have received a spirit of adoption.” The Holy Spirit, given to us in Baptism, does not make us servants of a distant master; he makes us sons and daughters, so that we dare to say what Jesus said in Gethsemane: “Abba! Father!” It is “that very Spirit bearing witness with our spirit that we are children of God, and if children, then heirs, heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ.” Here is the Trinity at prayer within us: the Spirit, in us, crying to the Father, with the voice of the Son. We are not outside the mystery looking in. We have been taken inside it.

The Gospel is the last scene of Matthew. The eleven disciples go to the mountain in Galilee where Jesus had told them to go. “When they saw him, they worshiped him; but some doubted.” Even at the end, faith and hesitation stand side by side, and Jesus does not wait for perfect disciples. He comes near and says: “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.” Notice the singular: in the name, not the names. One God, one name, three Persons. Then comes the promise that closes the whole Gospel: “And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.” Matthew's Gospel began with Emmanuel, God with us (1:23); it ends with the same promise. The Trinity is not a God who keeps himself far away. The Father sent the Son; the Son sends us; the Spirit makes us children; and the risen Lord remains with us every day. As St Gregory of Nazianzus put it (in substance), no sooner do I think of the One than I am surrounded by the splendour of the Three; no sooner do I distinguish the Three than I am carried back to the One.
conn: Deuteronomy 4.

Part of Moses' first great speech on the plains of Moab, before Israel enters the land. It looks back on the Exodus and on Sinai (called Horeb in Deuteronomy) to call Israel to faithfulness. Two chapters later comes the Shema: “Hear, O Israel: The Lord is our God, the Lord alone” (Deuteronomy 6:4), which Jesus himself called the first commandment (Mark 12:29).
The voice out of the fire.

At Horeb the people heard the voice of God from the midst of the fire on the mountain and lived (Deuteronomy 4:12, 33; 5:24). God speaks, but he is not seen; Israel was to make no image of him (4:15–16).
Psalm 33:6.

“By the word of the Lord … and by the breath of his mouth.” The Hebrew word for breath is ruach, also the word for Spirit. Many Fathers, among them St Irenaeus, saw here the Word and the Spirit as the “two hands” of the Father in creation.
“Abba.”

An Aramaic word for “father,” used by Jesus in Gethsemane (Mark 14:36). Paul keeps the Aramaic word in Greek letters here and in Galatians 4:6, a sign that the first Christians treasured the very word Jesus used.
Adoption.
In Roman law an adopted son received the full name, rights and inheritance of his new father. Paul uses the image to say that in Christ we truly share the Son's relationship with the Father.
“Some doubted.”
The Greek word (edistasan) appears in Matthew only here and in 14:31, when Peter sinks in the waves and Jesus says, “You of little faith, why did you doubt?” It means hesitation more than unbelief.
“In the name.”

The command to baptise “in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit” is the oldest Trinitarian formula of the Church; it is also given in the Didache (chapter 7), a Christian writing of the late first or early second century.
Nicaea and Constantinople.

The Creed we profess today was formulated at the Councils of Nicaea (325) and Constantinople (381), which confessed the Son “consubstantial with the Father” and the Holy Spirit as “the Lord, the giver of life … who with the Father and the Son is adored and glorified.”
Trinity Sunday.
A feast of the Holy Trinity was kept in many places in the Middle Ages; Pope John XXII extended it to the whole Latin Church in 1334, on the Sunday after Pentecost.
An Indian voice.

Brahmabandhab Upadhyay (1861–1907), a Bengali Catholic, wrote a Sanskrit hymn to the Trinity, “Vande Saccidanandam,” using the Indian words for being, consciousness and bliss. He did not claim that the Hindu idea and the Christian mystery are the same; he tried to praise the Trinity in words his people could feel.
altar: Every Mass is the prayer of the Trinity. We begin “in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit”; the Eucharistic Prayer is addressed to the Father, through the Son, in the Holy Spirit, who is called down upon the gifts to make them the Body and Blood of Christ; and it ends: “Through him, and with him, and in him, O God, almighty Father, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, all glory and honour is yours.”

In Holy Communion the promise of today's Gospel takes flesh: “I am with you always.” The Son, really present, comes to dwell in us; and where the Son is, the Father and the Spirit are, for the three Persons are never separated. Each Communion draws us deeper into the life of the Trinity.
outline: Make the sign of the cross slowly with everyone. Ask: how many times have I done this without thinking of what I am saying?
Point 1 · Has anything so great ever happened?
The God of Israel speaks, chooses and rescues.
One God: the Trinity is not three gods but the one God revealed in his inner life.
The Spirit makes us children and prays in us.
Baptised into the Trinity, sent to all nations, never alone.
A child running into the arms of a father, while the mother laughs nearby: love given, love received, love shared.
“I am with you always, to the end of the age.”
live: Make the sign of the cross with meaning
Each time you sign yourself this week, pause for a breath on each name: Father, Son, Holy Spirit.
Spend five minutes each day simply saying, slowly and from the heart, “Abba, Father,” and let the Spirit pray in you.
Find out the date of your Baptism and mark it in your calendar; on that day, thank God, renew your baptismal promises, and visit the font if you can.
Share your faith this week with one person who is searching: a word, an invitation to Mass, a book, a prayer together.
fathers: Above all, guard this great deposit of faith, for which I live and fight: the profession of faith in the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. I give you one Godhead and power, found in the Three, and containing the Three in a distinct way (Oration 40, quoted in CCC 256).

If you see love, you see the Trinity. For love means one who loves, the one who is loved, and love itself. Look into your own heart: there you will find an image, faint but true, of the God who is love (On the Trinity, Book 8).

The Father does all things through the Word in the Holy Spirit; in this way the unity of the Holy Trinity is preserved, and one God is preached in the Church, who is over all, and through all, and in all (Letters to Serapion).

Keep, I pray you, this faith of mine undefiled, and grant me to the end of my life the voice of my conscience, so that I may always hold fast to what I professed when I was baptised in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit (On the Trinity, Book 12).
magis: The mystery of the Most Holy Trinity is the central mystery of Christian faith and life, the mystery of God in himself, the source of all the other mysteries of faith.

The Trinity is One: not three gods but one God in three Persons, the “consubstantial Trinity.” The divine Persons are really distinct from one another by their relations of origin, and they are relative to one another.

The whole divine economy is the common work of the three Persons. The ultimate end of that economy is that we be drawn into the perfect unity of the Blessed Trinity; even now we are called to be a dwelling for the Trinity.

The mission of the Church comes from the eternal love of the Holy Trinity: she is sent to make disciples of all nations so that all may share the communion of the Father and the Son in their Spirit of love.
The universal Church is “a people made one with the unity of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit” (quoting St Cyprian).
Dominum et Vivificantem 10 (St John Paul II, 1986)
In his intimate life God “is love,” and the Holy Spirit is personal love, the Person-Love and the Person-Gift of the Father and the Son.
saints: A Carmelite nun of Dijon in France, who died at twenty-six and was canonised by Pope Francis in 2016. Her prayer, “O my God, Trinity whom I adore,” is quoted by the Catechism (CCC 260). She wanted her whole life to be a “praise of glory” to the Trinity dwelling in her soul.

2027-05-23.prayer: God our Father, you sent into the world the Word of truth and the Spirit of sanctification, and so made known to us your wonderful mystery. Lord Jesus Christ, eternal Son, you have made us children of your Father and you remain with us always, to the end of the age. Holy Spirit, Lord and giver of life, you cry in our hearts “Abba! Father!” and bear witness that we are children of God. Most Holy Trinity, one God, we adore you, we praise you, we thank you. Keep us faithful to the faith of our Baptism, make our families and our parish an image of your communion of love, and send us to make disciples of all nations. With the Blessed Virgin Mary, daughter of the Father, mother of the Son and temple of the Holy Spirit, and with all the saints, we give you glory, now and for ever. Amen.

quick: Moses: has anything so great ever happened? The Lord is God in heaven and on earth; there is no other.
Paul: the Spirit makes us children of God; in us he cries “Abba! Father!”; we are heirs with Christ.
The risen Jesus sends the eleven to baptise all nations in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, and promises to be with us always.
2027-05-23.action: Make the sign of the cross slowly and with attention every time you pray this week.
2027-05-23.question: Do I live as a child of the Father, a brother or sister of the Son, and a temple of the Holy Spirit?
catechism: The Trinity, the central mystery of faith.
One God in three distinct Persons.
Called to be a dwelling of the Trinity.
kidsaint: St Patrick brought the Gospel to Ireland about sixteen hundred years ago. A well-loved story, told many centuries after him, says that he picked up a shamrock, a little plant with three leaves on one stem, to explain the Holy Trinity: three leaves, yet one plant. No picture can fully show who God is, but the story helped people remember that God is one, and that there are three Persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Lesson: we can learn about God even from small things in nature.
2027-05-23.special: Solemnity of the Most Holy Trinity, Year B: Gloria and Creed; it takes the place of the Eighth Sunday in Ordinary Time; Angelus at noon.
term: From the Latin consubstantialis, translating the Greek homoousios, the word chosen by the Council of Nicaea (325): the Son is of the same substance, the same being, as the Father. It says that the Son is truly God, not a lesser being, and is professed in the Creed at every Sunday Mass.

family.explain: God is one, but God is not lonely. God is the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, loving one another for ever. When we were baptised, we were welcomed into that family of love. That is why we make the sign of the cross: in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Our family, where we love and forgive each other, is meant to be a small picture of God's family.
family.intention: We pray for all children who will be baptised this year, for their parents and godparents, and for missionaries who bring the Gospel to all nations.
family.ask: Ask: “When is our family most like God's family of love?” Then make the sign of the cross together, slowly, and say what each name means to you.

illus: A catechism teacher in a parish near Mangaluru asked her class of ten-year-olds how God can be one and three. After many guesses, a quiet girl said: in our house there is my father, my mother and me. We are three. But when we sit together for prayer at night, we are one family, and it is the love that makes us one. The teacher told her that no picture of the Trinity is perfect, because God is not a family of three gods. But she added: you have understood the most important thing. God is love, and love is never alone.

pm.open: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, as it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
share: Has anything so great as this ever happened? (Deuteronomy 4:32). What great things has God done in my life that I should remember today?
When we cry, “Abba! Father!” it is that very Spirit bearing witness with our spirit that we are children of God (Romans 8:15–16). Do I pray as a child, or as a stranger?
I am with you always, to the end of the age (Matthew 28:20). Where do I need to remember this promise this week?
pm.resp: Blessed the people the Lord has chosen to be his own.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a sign of the communion of the Holy Trinity in the world.
For all who will be baptised this year, and for their parents and godparents.
For missionaries, catechists and all who make disciples of all nations.
For families, that they may grow as communities of love, an image of the Trinity.
For those who doubt, that the risen Lord may come near to them as he came to the eleven.
For our group, that the Spirit may teach us to pray “Abba, Father” with trust.
pm.close: Most Holy Trinity, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, one God, we adore you and give you thanks; keep us always in your love. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the first thing most of us learned as children in church was not a prayer but a gesture. Our mother or grandmother took our small hand and made it touch the forehead, the chest, the left shoulder and the right: in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Today the Church celebrates what that gesture means: the Most Holy Trinity.

We cannot fully understand God. If we could, he would be smaller than our minds. But God has not left us in the dark. In the first reading Moses tells Israel: ask from one end of heaven to the other: has anything so great as this ever happened? The God who spoke from the fire, who rescued his people from Egypt, is the one true God. So acknowledge today and take to heart that the Lord is God in heaven above and on the earth beneath; there is no other (Deuteronomy 4:39). We Christians believe in one God, not three.

But Jesus has shown us the inner life of this one God. He calls God his Father. He promises the Holy Spirit. And St Paul tells us that this Spirit has been given to us: you have received a spirit of adoption. When we cry, “Abba! Father!” it is that very Spirit bearing witness with our spirit that we are children of God (Romans 8:15–16). Think of that. The Spirit, inside you, praying to the Father with the words of the Son. You are not outside the Trinity looking in; you have been brought inside.

In the Gospel the risen Jesus sends the disciples: go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit (Matthew 28:19). Notice that some of them doubted. Jesus sent them anyway. He does not wait for perfect people. Neither should we wait until we have perfect faith before we share it.

What does the Trinity mean for our daily life? God is a communion of love: the Father loves the Son, the Son loves the Father, and the Holy Spirit is their love in Person. We are made in that image. A family where husband and wife forgive each other, where children are welcomed, where the old are cared for, is a small picture of God. A parish where people of different backgrounds pray and serve together is a picture of God. Selfishness, division, loneliness by choice, these are not God's image.

And finally, Jesus gives the promise that ends Matthew's Gospel: remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age (Matthew 28:20). In every Mass he keeps that promise, coming to us in his Body and Blood. So today, let us make the sign of the cross slowly, with love, and let us live as children of the Father, brothers and sisters of the Son, and temples of the Holy Spirit. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Amen.
kids: Children, let us make the sign of the cross together, slowly: in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. There is one God, and God is three Persons: the Father who made us, Jesus the Son who saved us, and the Holy Spirit who lives in our hearts.

God is like a family of love that never ends. When you were baptised, God made you part of his family! So every time you make the sign of the cross, you can say: thank you, God, for making me your child.

opts.a: Heirs of God, not slaves of fear
intro: Paul tells the Romans that those led by the Spirit are children of God, and if children, then heirs. The Trinity is not only a mystery to believe but a family that makes us heirs.

sub: As he led Israel in the desert.
points.apply: Before each decision this week, ask the Spirit to lead you.
Name one fear and hand it over to the Father in prayer.
Offer one suffering this week united with Christ.

concl: Through the Son and in the Spirit we become heirs of the Father.
Children of God need not live in fear.
opts.resolve: This week I will let the Spirit lead my decisions and hand my fears to the Father.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the mystery of the Holy Trinity can seem far above us. But St Paul shows us that the Trinity is not only something to think about; it is a family into which we have been brought. For all who are led by the Spirit of God are children of God (Romans 8:14).

Led by the Spirit. Isaiah remembered how God guided Israel in the desert: the spirit of the LORD gave them rest. Thus you led your people (Isaiah 63:14). The Spirit is not only a gift we received at Baptism; he is a guide who walks with us each day. When we must decide something about work, family, marriage or money, we can ask: Holy Spirit, lead me.

Paul continues: for you did not receive a spirit of slavery to fall back into fear (Romans 8:15). Many Christians live as if God were a harsh master waiting to punish them. But we are not slaves; we are sons and daughters. When Israel stood trapped at the Red Sea, Moses said: do not be afraid, stand firm, and see the deliverance that the LORD will accomplish for you today (Exodus 14:13). Children of the Father can face life without fear.

And then the greatest promise: if children, then heirs, heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ, if, in fact, we suffer with him so that we may also be glorified with him (Romans 8:17). What do we inherit? Not land or money, but God himself, the life of the Trinity for ever. The path to that inheritance passes through suffering with Christ. But God promises: when you pass through the waters, I will be with you (Isaiah 43:2).

So today let us live as heirs, not slaves. Let the Spirit lead you. Hand your fears to the Father. Unite your sufferings with the Son. And when we make the sign of the cross at this Mass, let us remember that we are signed with the name of the family to which we belong. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Amen.

intro: Every prayer of the Church is shaped by the Trinity: to the Father, through the Son, in the Holy Spirit. Today we learn to pray as the Church prays.

points.h: To the Father, through the Son, in the Spirit
sub: The pattern of the Church's prayer.
The great Doxology of the Mass.
points.apply: Pay attention to the endings of the prayers at the Mass this Sunday.
Pray the Glory Be slowly after every decade of the Rosary this week.
Teach a child to make the sign of the cross and pray the Glory Be.

concl: Our prayer is a share in the life of the Trinity.
We pray to the Father, through the Son, in the Spirit, and live what we pray.
opts.resolve: This week I will pray the Glory Be with attention and teach it to a child.
homily: Dear friends, have you ever noticed how the prayers at Mass end? The priest prays to the Father, and then concludes: through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit. Every prayer of the Church has this shape: to the Father, through the Son, in the Spirit. St Paul explains why: for through him both of us have access in one Spirit to the Father (Ephesians 2:18).

We do not pray to a distant God from outside. Through Jesus, and with the Holy Spirit in our hearts, we pray from inside the family of God. Even creation was made this way: by the word of the LORD the heavens were made, and all their host by the breath of his mouth (Psalm 33:6). The Father creates through his Word and by his Breath. At the end of the Eucharistic Prayer, the priest lifts the Body and Blood of Christ and sings: through him, and with him, and in him, O God, almighty Father, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, all glory and honour is yours. And we answer with the great Amen.

Isaiah saw the Lord in the temple, and the seraphim crying: holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory (Isaiah 6:3). John heard the same song in heaven (Revelation 4:8). We sing it at every Mass in the Sanctus. This is prayer that asks for nothing; it simply adores. The Glory Be is the same kind of prayer. We say it so quickly. Let us learn to say it slowly, with love.

Jesus sent his disciples to baptise in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and also: teaching them to obey everything that I have commanded you (Matthew 28:20). Moses had said: keep his statutes and his commandments… for your own well-being and that of your descendants after you (Deuteronomy 4:40). Prayer to the Trinity must become a life of love: in our families, in forgiveness, in care for one another.

So this week, let us listen carefully to the prayers at the Mass. Let us say the Glory Be slowly. And let us teach a child to make the sign of the cross and to pray: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, as it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

intro: Theme: “In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.”
The God of Israel who speaks and saves, the one God besides whom there is no other, the Spirit who makes us children, and the mission given in the one Name.

points.h: Has anything so great ever happened?
sub: Ask from one end of heaven to the other.
The voice out of the fire.
A God who chooses and rescues.
q: has anything so great as this ever happened or has its like ever been heard of?
No one has ever seen God. It is God the only Son, who is close to the Father's heart, who has made him known.
points.apply: Write down three great things God has done in your life and thank him for each before Sunday ends.

sub: Israel's confession of the one God.
One God revealed in his inner life.
q: So acknowledge today and take to heart that the Lord is God in heaven above and on the earth beneath; there is no other.
yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things and for whom we exist, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things and through whom we exist.
points.apply: Pray the Creed slowly once this week at home, pausing on each article about the Father, the Son and the Spirit.

q: When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.

For you did not receive a spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you have received a spirit of adoption. When we cry, “Abba! Father!” it is that very Spirit bearing witness with our spirit that we are children of God.
points.apply: Begin each prayer this week with the word “Abba” and a moment of trust.

sub: Worship and doubt on the mountain.
q: And one called to another and said: “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.”

Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything that I have commanded you. And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
points.apply: Find the date of your Baptism, and invite one person who is searching to come with you to Mass.

concl: The Trinity is not a riddle but the life of the one God, revealed in history and opened to us in Christ.
Baptised in the one Name, we are children of the Father, brothers and sisters of the Son and temples of the Spirit, sent to all nations with the Lord who is with us always.
2027-05-23.resolve: Make the sign of the cross slowly and with love every time you pray this week, and renew your baptismal promises on Sunday evening.
